questions.question: In story S11 (Decline durability (D7)), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/pendingDirectInviteStorage.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/declineDurability.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/invitations/declineDurability*.test.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/invitations/declineDurability.harness.test.ts and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `invitations` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S11 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S11's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/pendingDirectInviteStorage.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/declineDurability.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/invitations/declineDurability*.test.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/invitations/declineDurability.harness.test.ts)? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S11 implementation match the intent of its scope (pending-direct-invite marker extended with inviteeRef and declined flag (legacy ignored), welcomeDeclined marks declined durably, removal after await group.synced() outside the listener, startup retry of every declined marker, clear marker and send exactly one declined announcement only after remove) and respect its exclusions (Cancel-invitation UI path (S14))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S11 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

Seam contract PendingDirectInviteMarker (consumed beyond S11; consumers: S14): does the delivered artifact at app/src/lib/marmot/pendingDirectInviteStorage.ts expose exactly the declared shape (fields: inviteeRef: string; pubkey: string; declined: boolean) and uphold each invariant (inviteeRef persisted at invite time; declined set durably before any removal work; marker cleared only after removeMember resolves; legacy markers without inviteeRef are ignored without throwing)? Show the type/definition with file:line and a test asserting each invariant, including enum/constant membership and value ranges where the contract constrains them.

AC-DECL-1: At invite time the sponsor MUST persist `inviteeRef → pubkey` in the pending-direct-invite marker. On `welcomeDeclined` the marker MUST be set `declined` durably before any removal work. The removal MUST run outside the listener frame after `await group.synced()`, and at startup MUST be retried for every `declined` marker. The marker MUST be cleared and the `declined` announcement sent only after `removeMember` resolved. Tests: (a) decline while group unsynced → `removeMember` call occurs only after `synced()` resolves; (b) decline while sponsor offline (listener fired, process restarts with marker in idb) → startup retry calls `removeMember`; (c) `removeMember` rejects → marker stays `declined`, no announcement; (d) success → marker cleared and exactly one announcement. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness; e2e:groups-direct-invite-lifecycle, groups-invite-lifecycle-announcements (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-DECL-2: A `welcomeDeclined` event with an unknown `inviteeRef` MUST be ignored (no `removeMember`). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-DEL-2: Pending-direct-invite marker shape MUST carry `inviteeRef` and a `declined` flag; legacy markers without `inviteeRef` MUST be ignored without throwing (pre-alpha, no migration). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

declineDurability.ts runs the removal outside the client listener: onWelcomeDeclined makes no client call and enqueues on handle.enqueue as its LAST action, and the removal is only STARTED from the job (detached, tracked by idle()) so one group's bounded synced() wait (30 s) cannot stall the serial client job queue behind it. Confirm with file:line (declineDurability.ts onWelcomeDeclined / start) and the tests 'the removal is not in the listener frame' and 'a slow removal never holds the client job queue' in declineDurability.test.ts.

Announcement ordering and delivery guarantee: marker is cleared BEFORE the declined announcement, the announcement is best-effort and never retried (at-most-once), and an invitee already absent from the member list resolves as already-removed with no second Remove and no announcement. Confirm the trade-off (a crash between clear and announce loses the cosmetic post, a crash between removeMember and clear never duplicates it) is the intended reading of AC-DECL-1 'cleared and announced only after removeMember resolved', and that tests 'a lost marker clear ... already-removed' and 'a failing announcement ...' pin it.

Trust boundary of welcomeDeclined: the payload comes from the library (decline rumor authenticated by the seal), and the app only acts on a marker that THIS sponsor wrote at invite time and that carries exactly that inviteeRef within that group; an unknown ref, a ref of another group, a pubkey- or key-shaped ref and malformed payloads write and remove nothing. Show markPendingDirectInviteDeclined (pendingDirectInviteStorage.ts) and the tests 'a hostile inviteeRef that merely resembles a pubkey or key cannot select a marker' and 'no removeMember ... for an unknown ref, another group's ref, malformed payloads'. Also confirm the announcement is an MLS group rumor via the injected announce port (never a public publish) and carries only the invitee pubkey.

declineDurability.harness.test.ts uses REAL Alice/Bob clients over FakeRelay + createMemoryStorage with the real idb-keyval marker store. Confirm: (1) the real group's synced() settles before removeMember and the announcement follows removeMember's resolution (trace order through a delegating observer, not a mock); (2) the offline/reload variant drops the queued job, tears Alice down, restarts a new client over the SAME storage and the same idb and the startup retry removes Bob and announces once, a second retry does nothing; (3) the unknown-ref case leaves Bob a member. In-place mutants (announce always, clear on failure, startup no-op, no already-removed check, removal not waiting for the durable mark, legacy accepted, announce before remove, mark ignoring the ref, skipSync) were each killed.

Scope notes: (a) invitations/index.ts (barrel) was edited although not in scope.includes, as S8/S10 did, because other modules import the invitations module only through its index; (b) the legacy writer markPendingDirectInvite (bare true) and the presence-only readers are kept for the not-yet-cut-over call site (InviteMemberModal, MarmotContext) and removed by S18/S22; record-aware readers ignore bare-true markers; (c) S18 must wire createMarkerRecordingInviter around the inviter, route clientEvents.welcomeDeclined to onWelcomeDeclined, and call startupRetry() once after bootstrap with announce bound to the S6 sender (kind 9); S14's cancel invitation and S17's wipe clear markers through clearPendingDirectInvite / clearAllPendingDirectInvites.
